categories.name: It works
categories.notes: dotnet build has 0 errors and 0 warnings. / returns 200 through the '/' domain on the Blog page, not WWW. It lists both posts newest first, as cards with a listing image, date, title, excerpt and link, and the links work. Both posts render all 5 blocks (3 rich text, 1 image, 1 quote) with no 'Could not render component'. All 7 images are provided Unsplash photos imported over MCP into a 'Blog' media folder, served through signed GetCropUrl URLs that load. All pages are published.

categories.name: Content modeling
categories.notes: richTextBlock, imageBlock (image, caption) and quoteBlock (quote, attribution) are element types in Blocks. blogFrontPage and blogPost are documents in Pages. siteRoot (Repositories) is the only root type and allows only blogFrontPage, and blogFrontPage allows only blogPost. Templates are assigned as allowed and default, under a shared layout master. The one custom data type, 'Blog Body Grid', sits under Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid and is the 'blocks' body on both page types. Post metadata (title, publishDate, excerpt, listingImage) are real properties. No compositions, and no duplicated or orphaned types. Nit: imageBlock has no alt-text property, so the caption doubles as alt.

categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: blogFrontPage.cshtml and blogPost.cshtml use Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model, "blocks"), and the scaffold's blockgrid partials are untouched. There are 3 markup-free adapters at Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml. Each takes BlockGridItem<T>, maps it to a plain model in Models/Blocks and calls Component.InvokeAsync. Each of the 3 ViewComponents (Image, Quote, RichText) renders Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml using only its plain model. Program.cs and appsettings.json are unchanged, and there are no migrations. Friendly extensions (Children<T>, AncestorOrSelf<T>, Url(), GetCropUrl) are used with nothing injected. Styling is Tailwind compiled to wwwroot/dist/site.css. The .mcp.json diff comes from the bench's mcp-guided setup, not from the model.

categories.name: Content & presentation
categories.notes: Two on-topic, accurate posts of about 450 words each. 'MCP Is the USB-C of AI' covers the M×N to M+N integration problem, self-describing servers and the value of a 'boring' standard. 'Why MCP Makes Your CMS Talk Back' covers this site being built over MCP, the split between dev and editor servers, and conventions. Each post has 6-7 paragraphs over 3 rich text blocks with h2 subheads, plus a pull quote and a relevant photo with a correct photographer credit. The front page has an intro, a hero photo and a 2-column card grid. Post pages are readable at max-w-3xl, with a date, lede, hero image, styled quote and back link.

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes: 64 Umbraco MCP calls (37 writes), with no browser, migration, Management API, uSync or database use. Schema and media went through 'umbraco', and pages, blocks and publishing through 'umbraco-editor'. The model followed the 12 steps in order: model, media, content, domain, stop and build, Razor, npm build, rebuild and restart, curl checks. Its only extra was a read-only MCP probe before 'dotnet run', which answered because Umbraco was already up. No memory access and no bench-folder reads. It wrote scratch curl output (page.html) to /tmp, outside the project folder: small deduction, the same as earlier runs (2/3). The final report is accurate (2/2) and discloses the 'Publish cancelled' on the descendant publish, empty publishedUrls from get-page and the unchecked uSync export.

summary: A clean, complete MCP-built blog. It has 3 blocks (rich text, image, quote) on one block grid used by both page types, a front page with a card listing and two substantive posts of 5 blocks each. The Razor follows the adapter → ViewComponent pipeline exactly, and every check passes.
strengths: Schema, media and content built entirely over the two MCP servers, following the 12 steps in order
Textbook rendering pipeline: GetBlockGridHtmlAsync, markup-free adapters, plain models in Models/Blocks, one ViewComponent per block
Correct folders, allowed children, templates on a shared layout, domain '/' on the front page
Substantive, accurate posts with h2 subheads, pull quotes and correctly credited Unsplash photos
Polished Tailwind design, and an honest final report

issues.text: imageBlock has no alt-text property, so the caption ('… Photo: X on Unsplash') is used as alt (Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/imageBlock.cshtml)
The post hero (listingImage) has no photographer credit, unlike the inline image blocks (Views/blogPost.cshtml)
